forms.when: When asking someone for permission (될까요 is more polite)
forms.means: May I…? Is it okay if I…?

forms.when: When stating rules, prohibitions, or warnings

forms.means: don’t have to / it’s not necessary to

task.title: Make Library Rules
task.line: Write 2 things you may do and 2 things you must not do in the library, using -아/어도 돼요 and -(으)면 안 돼요.

title: Permission and Prohibition: -아/어도 되다, -(으)면 안 되다, and distinguishing ‘안 V-아/어도 되다’
watchOut: ‘안 V-아/어도 돼요’ (don’t have to) ≠ ‘V-(으)면 안 돼요’ (must not). E.g. 우산을 안 써도 돼요 (you don’t need an umbrella; it isn’t raining) vs 우산을 쓰면 안 돼요 (you are not allowed to use an umbrella).
Position of 안: put ‘안’ directly before the verb. E.g. 약을 안 먹어도 돼요 (you don’t need to take medicine) ≠ 약을 먹어도 안 돼요 (different meaning: even if you take medicine, it doesn’t help).
Watch the conjugation: 하다→해도, 마시다→마셔도, 쓰다→써도 (ㅡ drops), 듣다→들어도 (ㄷ irregular).
